text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- British Bass' expected acquisition of U.K. brewery joint venture Carlsberg-Tetley could be postponed until after British elections to be held in May at the latest. The takeover is currently being reviewed by Britain's Monopolies & Mergers Commission.
--- Danish electronics company Terma Elektronik A/S has won an order from the U.S. Air Force worth 250 million crowns to supply 800 aircraft with advanced electronic equipment.
--- Food minister Henrik Dam Kristensen refuses to close Danish-German borders for pig trucks despite swine fever in Germany and the Netherlands.
--- Denmark's health authorities are to tighten hygiene control on Copenhagen's 1,200 restaurants after food poisoning cases increased to 117 in 1996 from 63 in the previous year.

--- Political experts see Russia exerting pressure on Denmark because of its support for the Baltic states' membership of NATO and President Clinton's visit to Denmark next month, which is seen as recognition of Denmark as one of the United States' closest allies.

--- Denmark is to maintain investments in China worth billions of crowns despite insecurity after the death of Deng Xiaoping, but new sales offensives could be postponed until the political situation is clarified.
--- After years of solid advances, Danish banks face tougher times with more staff cuts, mergers and alliances.
